minutes.headline: Water commissioners again declined to move on a Howard Street water extension, asking O'Brien's attorney for a written opinion first.
minutes.summary: The board heard a resident whose self-made service line repair was done without inspection, and agreed to a no-charge leak test and to draft a repair-inspection regulation. It then heard Kevin O'Brien's renewed request for water for his Howard Street project; the board asked his attorney to put an opinion in writing for review by district counsel, with a straw poll leaning against. It also set a January special district meeting for KP Law invoices and a Lancaster pilot study.

public_comment.topic: Objected to sending the O'Brien water request to counsel again; said voters and the state have already acted and the answer should be no.
Mr O'Brien briefly said he has the right to be here and would have his attorney put a position in writing.
Asked what happened with the audit and the missed law firm invoices; discussed staffing and billing systems.

what_happened.line: Water commissioners again held off on a Howard Street water extension and asked Kevin O'Brien's attorney for a written opinion for district counsel to review.

The board set a special district meeting for January 10th at 6 p.m. to cover unpaid KP Law invoices and a pilot study appropriation for the Lancaster Avenue wells; the vote on the motion was not audible.
After a resident's self-repaired service line leaked, staff agreed to a no-charge leak test, and the superintendent was asked to draft a regulation requiring inspection of service line repairs.
Members voiced concern about recent legal spending and asked that O'Brien's attorney carry the burden of making the case.
The superintendent said the district could receive PFAS class action settlement money, with the amount uncertain, and that it should go to PFAS remediation.

why_it_matters: Whether the district extends water to the Howard Street project is still undecided, and the legal opinions it has requested draw on district spending on counsel.

Unpaid KP Law invoices and the Lancaster Avenue pilot testing must be funded by voters at a special district meeting, because the prior year's budget is closed and ARPA funds were not available for the testing.
A proposed inspection regulation for service line repairs could change what residents who repair their own lines must do and what they may be charged.
